description: We’re a creative team passionate about space, gaming, and technology, building an exciting space-themed game full of exploration and adventure. We’re looking for teammates skilled in game logic, problem-solving, storytelling, and game design. Creativity, teamwork, and a willingness to learn are what matter most. Join us and create something out of this world!
summary: Mission Forge is an interactive space mission design and simulation game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It challenges players to experience the complexities of real-world space missions by designing satellites, managing engineering constraints, and collaborating to achieve mission success. Players can explore missions solo with AI crewmates or work together in four-player cooperative mode. From selecting scientific instruments and balancing mass, power, thermal, and communication systems to passing GO / NO-GO reviews, launching spacecraft, and managing unexpected operational challenges, every decision has consequences. Incorporating real NASA mission information and space science data, Mission Forge transforms complex aerospace engineering concepts into an engaging, educational gaming experience. Through interactive mission control dashboards and post-mission debriefings, players learn how engineering decisions shape the success or failure of space missions.
details:
Project Details – Mission Forge (GO / NO-GO)

Mission Forge, featuring our game GO / NO-GO, is an interactive space mission design and simulation game that introduces players to the challenges of planning and operating real-world space missions. Players take on the role of a mission team, selecting scientific objectives, designing satellites, choosing instruments, and managing engineering constraints such as mass, power consumption, battery capacity, thermal requirements, communication systems, mission cost, and operational lifetime.

The game supports both solo gameplay, with AI crewmates, and four-player cooperative gameplay. Players must make engineering decisions, evaluate their spacecraft, and pass a GO / NO-GO review before launching. After launch, they monitor mission operations, respond to unexpected challenges, and see how their earlier decisions affect mission performance. The experience concludes with a mission debrief that helps players understand what worked, what failed, and why.

The primary benefit of Mission Forge is that it makes complex aerospace engineering concepts more accessible, interactive, and enjoyable. Instead of simply reading about satellites and space missions, players learn through experimentation and decision-making. Our intended impact is to encourage curiosity about space science, promote STEM education, and help people better understand the teamwork and engineering involved in exploring space.

For development, we used React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Node.js, Express, and Socket.IO, alongside shared game logic and data. We also incorporated real NASA-related mission information and space science data, drawing on sources including NASA, NASA/JPL-Caltech, NASA NSSDCA, and NASA CCMC (DONKI).

The creative aspect of our project is its combination of a cooperative game, spacecraft engineering, mission reviews, and operational simulation into one connected experience. We aimed to turn the decision-making process behind space missions into an engaging gameplay experience rather than a conventional educational presentation or static simulation.

Throughout development, our team considered scientific relevance, engineering constraints, gameplay balance, accessibility for players without an aerospace background, multiplayer collaboration, and the limited time available to complete a mission. We wanted to create something educational but also genuinely enjoyable, where every decision has meaningful consequences and players can experience the excitement and responsibility of running a space mission.
